entities.summary:
Claudian (b. 370 CE, Alexandria) was a journalist or media commentator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Alexandria. Known in the fields of poets & playwrights.

As a prominent figure in the Alexandrian literary scene, Claudian was influenced by the works of Homer and Hesiod, and his own compositions often explored themes of love, nature, and the human condition. His most famous work, the 'De Reditu Ad Ostium', is a poignant exploration of the transience of human life and the passage of time.

Claudian's significance extends beyond his literary output, as he provides valuable insights into the cultural and intellectual landscape of late antiquity. His writings also reflect the complex web of influences that shaped the Classical era, including the rise of Christianity and the decline of the Roman Empire.

Despite the passage of centuries, Claudian's work continues to captivate readers with its timeless themes and masterful use of language. His legacy serves as a testament to the enduring power of literature to transcend time and culture.

The average reading speed of an educated Roman citizen during Claudian's time was approximately 30-40 words per minute, a pace that would have allowed him to complete a 100-word poem in around 2.5-3 minutes.
